title: Indoor Turf in Northeast Florida | TIMELESS Grass & Greens
description: Indoor turf for gyms, studios and school spaces from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine Shores, planned around Florida’s floor-covering tests and fire review.
h1: Indoor turf in northeast Florida: know who reviews your floor first.
lede: Turf for gyms, studios and school spaces, matched to the fire tests for where it runs. We measure the space at a free visit, then give a written price.
wins: A free visit to measure the space
A custom layout you approve first

answer.question: What does indoor turf in a northeast Florida gym have to meet?
answer.answer: The floor-covering fire tests. Turf is made of fibers, so it must pass the pill test or ASTM D2859. In corridors, exit passageways and rooms open to a corridor, it also needs a Class II rating unless the building is fully sprinklered.

blocks.h2: Find the fire office that will look at your floor.
blocks.takeaway: The office that reviews your floor depends on the address, and Jacksonville and each county run their own. In a city like Fernandina Beach, ask its building department which fire office reviews it.
paras: The office that reviews your turf depends on the address. Under section 633.208, every city, county and special district with firesafety duties enforces the Florida Fire Prevention Code, and each may adopt stricter standards. Jacksonville adopts the current fire code as part of its building code and adds its own rules in Chapter 420 (Sec. 321.104).

In Clay County, the Fire Prevention Division handles plan reviews, fire permits and inspections for the unincorporated county, Green Cove Springs and Keystone Heights. In St. Johns County, the Fire Marshal’s Office is part of the review for building permits on commercial structures in the unincorporated county and in St. Augustine Beach. In Nassau County, the Building Department issues permits and reviews plans for the unincorporated county. Inside a city or town such as Fernandina Beach or Orange Park, ask its building department which fire office reviews the permit.

blocks.h2: Ask which code edition your permit will fall under.
blocks.takeaway: Florida's building code moves to its next edition on December 31, 2026, so ask the building department which one your permit falls under. The fire code's next edition has no date set yet.
paras: The building code is about to change. The Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023) took effect December 31, 2023, and St. Johns County lists it as the edition its building department enforces. The International Code Council’s Florida code library lists the 9th Edition, based on the 2024 International Building Code, as effective December 31, 2026. If your permit could land near that date, ask the building department which edition it will review.

The fire code’s next edition has no date yet. As of September 12, 2026, the adopted rule, in effect since December 31, 2023, makes the fire code the Florida 2021 editions of NFPA 1 and NFPA 101, the publications adopted in Rule 69A-60.005, and 16 chapters of uniform fire safety standards. The State Fire Marshal scheduled hearings on a 9th Edition for July 14, 2026, and FLRules lists the June 2026 proposed rule but no adopted version. Section 633.208 applies the fire code’s new-building rules by the date the building permit is issued, so ask the fire office which edition it will use for yours.

blocks.h2: Get test results for the turf and pad you’ll actually lay.
blocks.takeaway: The code doesn't name turf, but turf is made of fibers, so plan on the pill test with the pad you'll lay. Corridors and exit routes also need Class II unless fully sprinklered.
paras: Section 804 of the building code exempts wood, vinyl, linoleum, terrazzo and resilient floors that aren’t made of fibers. It doesn’t name turf, and turf is made of fibers, so plan on the floor-covering rules. Every floor covering must pass the DOC FF-1 pill test or ASTM D2859. Carpet-type coverings are tested as proposed for use, including underlayment, and test reports go to the building official on request. In an existing building, the Existing Building Code says new interior floor finish, including new carpeting, must comply with Section 804. Our turf fire article explains what the pill test does and doesn’t show.

Where the turf runs decides whether a pill-test pass is enough. Floors in stairway and ramp enclosures, exit passageways, corridors, and rooms not separated from a corridor by partitions running from the floor to the underside of the ceiling need a Class II rating, 0.22 watts per square centimeter or more, in assembly, business and educational groups. In a building with an automatic sprinkler system throughout, installed to the code’s standard, a pill-test pass is accepted where Class II is required. Show us the floor plan so the report matches where the turf goes.

blocks.h2: Your type of facility can add a permit or a second fire official.
blocks.takeaway: In Jacksonville, an assembly space for 50 or more needs a permit, so ask how the city counts your floor before you set an opening date. Public school gyms add a second fire official.
paras: A gymnasium without spectator seating is assembly Group A-3. Training and skill development outside a school program, including martial arts studios and gymnastics, is business Group B where it isn’t classified as assembly. A building or tenant space used for assembly with fewer than 50 occupants is Group B. The 50-person line matters in Jacksonville too: Sec. 420.212 says a place of assembly can’t be maintained, operated or used without a permit, and defines one as a room or space used for assembly or educational occupancy for 50 or more occupants. Ask the city how it will count your training floor before you set an opening date.

Public school and college gyms answer to a second fire official. One of the fire code’s uniform chapters, Chapter 69A-58, covers facilities under a district school board or a public college board of trustees. If the local fire official and the board’s fire official disagree, they settle it by agreement in favor of the requirement with the greatest degree of life safety, or an alternative with equivalent life safety and an equivalent method of construction. If they can’t agree, either may petition the State Fire Marshal’s division for a declaratory statement. For turf in a school gym or weight room, ask the district’s facilities office who reviews the plans before you pick a product.

blocks.h2: Settle the permit question before the turf ships.
blocks.takeaway: The new $7,500 permit exemption for single-family owners won't cover a gym. Bring the floor plan with corridors and exits marked, whether the building is sprinklered, and your occupancy classification to the free visit.
paras: Florida’s new $7,500 permit exemption won’t cover a gym. Since July 1, 2026, section 553.79 has required local governments to exempt work valued under $7,500 for owners of single-family homes and their contractors, and Clay County’s notice on the law describes it the same way. St. Johns County says permits are required for most improvements and that the property owner must determine whether one is needed. Nassau County’s Ordinance 2025-023 changed the administrative chapter of the building code and added permit exemptions, so ask its Building Department whether any fits a floor covering.

On the free visit we measure the space and check the ground the turf goes on. Bring the floor plan with corridors and exits marked, whether the building is sprinklered, the occupancy classification if you have it, and any landlord or school approval steps. You approve a custom layout before work starts, then we lay, seam and edge the turf and walk you through the care it needs. See indoor facility turf for the rest of the job, or the northeast Florida page for other turf we install here.

faq.q: Is artificial turf a carpet under Florida’s codes?
faq.a: Section 804 of the building code doesn’t name turf, and its exemption covers only floors that aren’t made of fibers. The federal carpet standard covers finished products made in whole or in part of fabric or related material and used as a floor covering, and it includes mats with natural or synthetic fibers above a set size. Ask your building official to confirm in writing how the office will treat the turf before you order.

faq.q: Does the fire code set its own floor rules?
faq.a: Ask your local fire official. The State Fire Marshal directs questions about how the fire code affects a specific building to the local fire official. Bring the test reports for the turf and pad together, and ask which floor-finish requirements the office will apply.
